example.prompt: In an intake system where a coarse prescreen protects an algae-removal microscreen, does water pass through the microscreen before or after the coarse prescreen?
example.explanation: A larger-pore prescreen is placed upstream so it captures coarser debris before the water reaches the finer microscreen.

example.prompt: In chemical coagulation with a hydrolyzing metal coagulant, is rapid mixing intended to disperse the chemical before or after its fast hydrolysis reaction is complete?
example.explanation: Rapid mixing must quickly disperse the coagulant throughout the water before the fast hydrolysis reaction finishes.

example.prompt: When excessive mixing shear breaks floc apart, does that floc breakage happen before or after initial floc formation?
example.explanation: Floc must first form from destabilized particles before excessive shear can break those aggregates apart.

example.prompt: In a dissolved air flotation unit, do air bubbles and floc particles meet in the contact zone before or after the clarified subnatant is drawn off near the basin floor?
example.explanation: Floc and microscopic air bubbles first meet in the DAF contact zone so float separates upward before clarified subnatant is collected below.

example.prompt: When a roughing filter is paired with a slow sand filter to prevent rapid head-loss buildup, is the roughing filter placed before or after the slow sand filter?
example.explanation: Roughing filters are installed upstream of slow sand filters to strip out coarse solids before they can clog the slow sand bed.

example.prompt: During an upward backwash of a granular media filter, does the wash water pass through the underdrain before or after expanding the filter media bed?
example.explanation: Backwash water enters through the underdrain at the bottom of the filter and distributes upward into the media bed.

example.prompt: In the described multi-media filter backwash sequence, does the reduced-rate wash phase for bed restratification occur before or after the main high-rate media expansion wash?
example.explanation: A lower backwash rate is applied at the end of the media wash so the fluidized grains settle and restratify by density and size.

example.prompt: In the described air-scour filter washing model, is air scouring performed before or after the fluidizing water wash that restratifies the media?
example.explanation: In this washing model, air scour loosens deposits first and a fluidizing water wash is applied afterward to clean and restratify the bed.

example.prompt: In a diatomaceous-earth filtration cycle, is the initial diatomite precoat applied to the septum before or after continuous body-feed addition during the filtration run?
example.explanation: An initial coat of diatomite is deposited on the support septum first, and continuous diatomite body feed supplements it during the filtration run.

example.prompt: In an upflow adsorption clarifier filled with buoyant plastic media, is the incoming water coagulated before or after it rises through the buoyant media bed to trap floc?
example.explanation: Incoming water is coagulated first so that destabilized floc particles can be trapped as the water rises through the buoyant plastic media.

example.prompt: In a membrane system removing dissolved iron and manganese by oxidation, does membrane filtration occur before or after oxidant reaction time and precipitate formation?
example.explanation: The oxidant requires reaction time to convert dissolved metals into solid precipitates before the membrane can physically filter them out.

example.prompt: In an ion-exchange water softener cycle, does brine regeneration displace calcium, iron, and manganese into spent brine before or after those ions have been captured on the resin?
example.explanation: During the service run, the resin captures hardness as well as dissolved iron and manganese; brine regeneration is applied afterward to displace those accumulated ions into spent brine.

example.prompt: In drinking-water disinfection practice, must primary disinfection achieve pathogen inactivation before or after treated water reaches the first consumer?
example.explanation: Primary disinfection is designed to inactivate pathogens in the treatment process before water is delivered to the first consumer.

example.prompt: In the chloramination reaction model, do combined chlorine species exist before or after free chlorine reacts with ammonia in the water?
example.explanation: Combined chlorine consists of chloramines that are formed when chlorine reacts with ammonia.

example.prompt: Following the path of water from a surface intake through a treatment plant to the distribution network, does low-lift pumping occur before or after high-lift pumping?
example.explanation: Low-lift pumps move raw water from the source into the treatment plant, whereas high-lift pumps deliver treated water into the distribution system afterward.

example.prompt: As treated drinking water travels from the treatment plant out to a distant customer tap in a low-usage zone, is its water age lower before or after residing in oversized distribution pipes?
example.explanation: Water age is the elapsed time spent in distribution, so water has a lower age before spending extended time in low-usage or oversized mains.

example.prompt: As chlorinated water travels through a pipe containing wall biofilm and bottom sediment, is the chlorine residual higher before or after reacting with the bulk water, sediment, and pipe wall?
example.explanation: Reactions with bulk-water compounds, sediment, and pipe-wall materials consume disinfectant, leaving a lower residual after contact.

example.prompt: For the portion of precipitation that infiltrates deeply enough to recharge groundwater, does the water pass through shallow soil before or after reaching the deeper aquifer?
example.explanation: Infiltrating water moves downward through the shallow soil zone first before penetrating deeper to recharge an underlying aquifer.

example.prompt: In a gaining stream reach where the adjacent water table is higher than the stream surface, does water reside in the adjacent aquifer before or after entering the stream channel through the streambed?
example.explanation: In a gaining reach, groundwater flows from the surrounding aquifer through the streambed and into the stream channel.

example.prompt: In the particle-bound phosphorus runoff pathway, does overland runoff carry soil particles into a surface-water body before or after phosphorus is attached to those land-surface soil particles?
example.explanation: Phosphorus bound to soil particles on land is subsequently transported into receiving surface waters when overland runoff erodes and carries those particles.

example.prompt: In the aquatic nutrient-assimilation pathway, is ammonia present in the aqueous phase before or after algae and aquatic plants take up that ammonia?
example.explanation: Dissolved ammonia in the water column is taken up and assimilated by aquatic plants and algae.

example.prompt: In direct atmospheric reaeration of a surface-water body, is oxygen gas in the atmosphere before or after it becomes dissolved oxygen incorporated in the water?
example.explanation: During atmospheric reaeration, oxygen gas moves across the air-water interface from the atmosphere into dissolved form in the water.

example.prompt: In photosynthetic oxygenation of surface water, is oxygen absorbed into the surrounding water before or after aquatic plants release that oxygen during photosynthesis?
example.explanation: Aquatic plants produce and release oxygen during photosynthesis first, and that released oxygen is then absorbed by the surrounding water.

example.prompt: In activated-carbon adsorption of trace organic contaminants, are the trace organics dissolved in the water phase before or after they adhere to the internal carbon surface?
example.explanation: Adsorption transfers trace organic substances from the liquid water phase onto the porous solid surface of the activated carbon.

example.prompt: In a reverse-osmosis or nanofiltration unit, does feed water reach the semipermeable membrane before or after splitting into separated permeate and reject concentrate streams?
example.explanation: Pressurized feed water arrives at the semipermeable membrane first, where it separates into membrane-passing permeate and retained concentrate.

example.prompt: When rainwater absorbs atmospheric carbon dioxide, is carbonic acid formed in the water before or after carbon dioxide gas enters the water from the atmosphere?
example.explanation: Atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolves into the water first and then reacts with water to form carbonic acid.

example.prompt: Under anaerobic sulfate-reducing groundwater conditions, is sulfur present as oxidized sulfate before or after it is transformed into reduced sulfide such as hydrogen sulfide?
example.explanation: In sulfate-reducing environments, oxidized sulfur in sulfate serves as the precursor that is microbially reduced into hydrogen sulfide.

example.prompt: Within the capture zone of an active groundwater supply well, is water located in the surrounding aquifer formation before or after entering the pumping well along the pressure gradient?
example.explanation: Pumping lowers pressure at the well, causing groundwater in the surrounding aquifer formation to flow toward and into the well.

example.prompt: In a flowing artesian well where the confined aquifer's piezometric level is above ground, does the water emerge at the land-surface wellhead before or after rising from the pressurized confined aquifer?
example.explanation: Natural pressure in the confined aquifer pushes water up the well bore so it emerges at the land surface afterward without a pump.

example.prompt: During coastal saltwater intrusion triggered by heavy freshwater pumping, is seawater located at the coastal boundary before or after migrating laterally into the freshwater aquifer zone?
example.explanation: When freshwater withdrawal lowers coastal aquifer heads, saltwater at the coastal boundary encroaches inward into the freshwater aquifer zone.

example.prompt: In the geogenic origin of groundwater mineral hardness, are calcium and magnesium carried as dissolved minerals in groundwater before or after water contacts and dissolves naturally occurring minerals in soil and rock?
example.explanation: Water moving through the subsurface first contacts mineral-bearing soil and rock, dissolving those minerals and carrying them into groundwater supplies.

example.prompt: When calcium-bearing hard water is heated and forms solid scale, is the calcium present as dissolved hardness in the water before or after becoming a solid calcium carbonate deposit?
example.explanation: Calcium hardness starts dissolved in the water and precipitates into solid calcium carbonate scale when the water is heated.

example.prompt: When corrosive drinking water leaches metal from susceptible service lines or premise plumbing, is the lead or copper part of the solid plumbing material before or after appearing as leached metal in the water supply?
example.explanation: Lead or copper resides in the susceptible pipe or fixture material first and transfers into the drinking water when contacted by corrosive water.

example.prompt: In a UV advanced-oxidation process (UV-AOP), are highly reactive radicals generated by the UV-oxidant reaction before or after those radicals oxidize organic contaminants in the water?
example.explanation: UV light reacts with an oxidant to generate radicals first, and those radicals subsequently oxidize organic contaminants.

example.prompt: In direct UV photolysis of an organic contaminant, is the organic molecule degraded before or after a UV photon is emitted by the lamp and absorbed?
example.explanation: UV lamps emit photons first, and those photons subsequently degrade susceptible organic contaminants upon absorption.

example.prompt: In a conventional plant where powdered activated carbon (PAC) slurry is added to the water, is the PAC dispersed into the water stream before or after being removed with particulates during clarification?
example.explanation: Powdered activated carbon is dispersed into the water upstream so it can adsorb contaminants before settling out with other particulates in clarification.

example.prompt: In a closed water parcel where heterotrophic bacteria decompose organic matter without reaeration, is dissolved oxygen higher before or after that bacterial decomposition?
example.explanation: Bacterial decomposition of organic material consumes dissolved oxygen from the water, leaving a lower concentration afterward.

example.prompt: In a direct filtration plant that uses chemical coagulation and flocculation without sedimentation, does coagulation destabilize particles before or after the water enters the granular filter media?
example.explanation: Coagulation destabilizes suspended colloids upstream so they can aggregate during flocculation and attach to the filter media in direct filtration.

example.prompt: In a conventional treatment train, is the settleable-solids load in the water stream lower before or after passing through the clarification process on its way to the filters?
example.explanation: Clarification removes settleable floc particles upstream of the filters, so the settleable-solids load is lower after clarification.

example.prompt: In a solids-contact clarifier, have the recirculated sludge particles been formed before or after the newly incoming coagulated water enters the contact zone?
example.explanation: A solids-contact unit mixes incoming coagulated water with previously formed sludge particles that are already present in the basin.

example.prompt: In a ballasted clarification unit, is microsand-enhanced flocculation performed before or after the water passes through the lamellar settling zone?
example.explanation: Ballasted clarification incorporates microsand during flocculation to weight the floc before it settles rapidly in the downstream lamellar settling section.

example.prompt: In a constant-rate filtration plant where a clearwell buffers varying distribution demand, does water pass through the constant-rate filter before or after entering the clearwell storage?
example.explanation: Filtered water discharges from the constant-rate filters into the clearwell, which then absorbs fluctuations in downstream distribution demand.

example.prompt: In a treatment plant that uses UV irradiation or ozone for primary pathogen inactivation and adds a secondary disinfectant to maintain a distribution residual, is the secondary residual maintained in the distribution pipes before or after primary disinfection at the plant?
example.explanation: Primary disinfection acts in the treatment process before the first consumer, while secondary disinfection maintains a protective residual afterward as water travels through the distribution system.

example.prompt: As the pH of a chlorinated water stream is lowered while keeping total free chlorine constant, is the proportion of hypochlorous acid relative to hypochlorite ion greater before or after the pH reduction?
example.explanation: Hypochlorous acid becomes the dominant form of free chlorine at lower pH values, so its share is greater after the pH is lowered.

example.prompt: When acid is added to an unbuffered water sample and increases its hydrogen-ion concentration, is the numerical pH value lower before or after the hydrogen-ion concentration rises?
example.explanation: Because pH is an inverse logarithmic expression of hydrogen-ion concentration, the pH value falls after the hydrogen-ion concentration rises.

example.prompt: In the formation of disinfection byproducts from natural organic matter, do trihalomethanes form before or after a chlorine-based disinfectant reacts with organic material in the water?
example.explanation: Trihalomethanes are chemical reaction products that form after chlorine-based disinfectants react with natural organic matter present in the water.

example.prompt: In a colorimetric DPD chlorine test on a water sample containing chlorine, does the pink colour develop in the sample vial before or after the DPD reagent reacts with the chlorine?
example.explanation: The DPD method is colorimetric; the pink colour develops after the added DPD reagent reacts with the chlorine in the sample.

example.prompt: As Suspended particles and corrosion products travel through low-velocity distribution mains and settle out, are they carried in the flowing water before or after accumulating as pipe bottom sediment?
example.explanation: Particles and corrosion products are first suspended or carried in the water and then settle onto the pipe floor to become distribution-system sediment.

example.prompt: When a high-velocity flow reversal near a storage tank scours settled material from the pipe invert, is that material resting as bottom sediment before or after the flow reversal mobilizes and spreads it?
example.explanation: Material accumulates as settled sediment during normal or low flows first, and a subsequent flow reversal near the storage facility mobilizes and spreads it into the water column.

example.prompt: In an aquatic sediment where microbes mineralize organic nitrogen into ammonia, is the nitrogen bound in accumulated organic sediment material before or after microbial mineralization produces ammonia?
example.explanation: During ammonification in sediment, microbes break down organic nitrogen present in accumulated organic matter and transform it into ammonia.

example.prompt: In an anion-exchange treatment vessel removing negatively charged contaminant ions from water, are the negatively charged contaminant ions dissolved in the feed water before or after they exchange onto the resin surface?
example.explanation: Anion exchange captures negatively charged contaminant ions from the incoming water and binds them onto the resin surface while releasing resin counterions.

example.prompt: Inside a spiral-wound membrane module after water crosses the membrane leaf, does the filtered water enter the permeate carrier fabric before or after reaching the central collector tube by inward spiral flow?
example.explanation: Once permeate passes through the membrane sheet into the permeate carrier, it spirals inward along the carrier fabric before discharging into the central collector tube.

example.prompt: In a surface-water intake arrangement using raw-water screens, does screening out large solids occur before or after the main treatment processes?
example.explanation: Raw-water screens remove large debris at the intake stage prior to the treatment units.

example.prompt: In a plant layout where inter-stage pumps move water between the flocculator and the sedimentation basin, does pump-induced floc breakage occur before or after the water leaves the flocculator?
example.explanation: Pumping water between the flocculator and the sedimentation basin subjects already-flocculated water to shear after it exits the flocculator.

example.prompt: During downward filtration through a traditional stratified dual-media bed containing anthracite and silica sand, does the water pass through the silica sand layer before or after the anthracite layer?
example.explanation: Because silica sand sits below the coarser anthracite or GAC layer in a traditional dual-media bed, downflowing water contacts the anthracite first and the sand afterward.

example.prompt: In a downflow granular filter whose underdrain uses a support-media layer to retain fine filter grains, does filtered water reach the underdrain before or after passing through the support media?
example.explanation: Support media sits between the fine filter media and the underdrain, so downward-flowing water passes through the support layer before entering the underdrain.

example.prompt: As water moves downward through a ripened slow sand filter, does it encounter the biologically active microbial zone before or after passing through the main sand bed?
example.explanation: Biological activity in a slow sand filter is concentrated in the upper sand microbial layer, which downflowing water contacts before the deeper sand.

example.prompt: In a treatment train that pairs ozonation with biological filtration so ozone converts natural organic matter into more readily biodegradable compounds for the biofilter's microbial film, does ozonation occur before or after the biofilter?
example.explanation: Ozone breaks down natural organic matter first so the microbial film in the biofilter can assimilate the resulting biodegradable fraction.

example.prompt: In a treatment train that uses a granular carbon contactor to remove remaining ozone so it does not harm the microbes in a biological filter, does water pass through the biological filter before or after the carbon contactor?
example.explanation: The granular carbon contactor sits upstream of the biological filter so remaining ozone is removed before the water reaches the sensitive biofilter microbes.

example.prompt: In the thermal reactivation cycle of spent granular activated carbon, are the spent carbon granules cleaned by heating before or after they are placed back into reuse?
example.explanation: Spent carbon granules undergo thermal cleaning by heating first so that adsorbed contaminants are removed before the reactivated carbon is reused.

example.prompt: In a raw-water blending model with all other conditions fixed, oxygen-rich surface water is mixed into groundwater containing dissolved iron and manganese. What can happen to those metals?

options.label: They can precipitate out of solution
They convert into nitrogen gas
They remain completely unaffected by oxygen

example.explanation: Blending oxygen-rich surface water with groundwater can cause dissolved iron or manganese to precipitate.

example.prompt: In an open water model at constant pressure with all other conditions fixed, water temperature decreases from warm to cold. How does the water's oxygen-holding capacity change?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: Cold water has a greater capacity to hold dissolved oxygen than warm water.

example.prompt: In a closed water volume with no re-aeration and all other conditions fixed, bacteria decompose organic material. What happens to the dissolved oxygen concentration?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Bacterial decomposition of organic material consumes dissolved oxygen from the water.

example.prompt: In an inline static mixer with fixed geometry and all other conditions constant, the water flow rate drops substantially. What happens to the mixing power delivered by the static mixer?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Because a static mixer relies on flow energy, its delivered mixing power can drop substantially when flow decreases.

example.prompt: In a flocculation basin where floc has already formed and all other conditions are fixed, mixing shear becomes excessive. What is the effect on the formed floc?

options.label: Already-formed floc can break apart
Floc permanently fuses into solid rock
Floc size remains completely unchanged

example.explanation: Excessive mixing shear can break apart floc particles that have already formed.

example.prompt: In a flocculation model with constant mixing intensity G and all other conditions fixed, the mixing duration t is increased. What happens to the combined Gt parameter?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: Because Gt incorporates both mixing intensity and the duration mixing is applied, increasing time at constant intensity increases Gt.

example.prompt: In a settling basin retrofit model with fixed footprint and all other conditions constant, tube or plate settlers are installed. What happens to the distance floc must fall before settling onto a surface?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Tube or plate settlers enlarge the effective settling area and shorten the vertical distance floc must fall.

example.prompt: In a settling basin model with fixed volume and flow and all other conditions constant, inlet distribution is made uniform across the basin width. What is the effect on hydraulic short-circuiting?

options.label: Hydraulic short-circuiting is reduced
Hydraulic short-circuiting is guaranteed to worsen
Inlet distribution has no hydraulic effect

example.explanation: Uniform inlet distribution helps a settling basin avoid hydraulic short-circuiting.

example.prompt: In a sludge-blanket clarifier with all other conditions fixed, water temperature or flow rate changes rapidly. How does this perturbation affect sludge-blanket clarifier operation?

options.label: Conditions become unfavourable for the sludge blanket
The clarifier automatically converts to slow sand filtration
The blanket becomes unaffected by hydraulics

example.explanation: Rapid changes in water temperature or flow rate can be unfavourable for maintaining a stable sludge-blanket clarifier.

example.prompt: In a slow sand filtration train treating water with coarse particles and all other conditions fixed, a roughing filter is placed upstream. What happens to the rate of head-loss growth in the slow sand filter?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Roughing filters remove coarse particles ahead of slow sand filters that would otherwise cause rapid head-loss growth.

example.prompt: In a granular filter with an underdrain that requires support media and all other conditions fixed, the support gravel layer is omitted. What can happen to the filter media grains?

options.label: Filter grains can pass into the underdrain
Filter grains dissolve into chlorine gas
Filter grains float out the overflow weir during filtration

example.explanation: Support media are needed over some underdrains to keep filter grains from passing into the underdrain.

example.prompt: In a filter backwash design model with identical grain size and all other conditions fixed, granular activated carbon is used instead of denser anthracite. How does the backwash rate needed for bed expansion change?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Granular activated carbon is less dense than anthracite and therefore needs a lower expansion backwash rate.

example.prompt: At the end of a multi-media filter wash cycle with all other conditions fixed, the wash water rate is lowered before shutting off. What does this lower wash rate allow the filter bed to do?

options.label: Restratify into its media layers
Remain permanently fluidized
Convert sand into activated carbon

example.explanation: Lowering the wash rate at the end of the media wash permits the expanded bed to restratify properly.

example.prompt: In a membrane filtration system with constant feed throughput and all other conditions fixed, backwash and reject-stream losses occur. How does net system output compare to feed throughput?

options.label: Net output is less than feed throughput
Net output exceeds feed throughput
Net output equals feed throughput

example.explanation: When backwash or reject-stream losses occur, a membrane system's net output is less than its feed throughput.

example.prompt: In a biological filtration train with all other conditions fixed, ozone pretreatment is applied to water containing natural organic matter ahead of the biofilter. What happens to the biodegradability of that organic matter?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: Ozone pretreatment can convert natural organic matter into more readily biodegradable material for a downstream biofilter.

example.prompt: In a chemical disinfection contactor with constant disinfectant residual concentration and all other conditions fixed, the effective contact time increases. What happens to the achieved CT value?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: For chemical disinfection, CT equals residual concentration multiplied by effective contact time, so increasing contact time at constant residual increases CT.

example.prompt: In a drinking-water system model where ozone or UV is used alone with no secondary chemical disinfectant added and all other conditions fixed, water enters the distribution system. What persistent disinfectant residual do ozone or UV themselves provide in distribution?

options.label: No persistent disinfectant residual is created by ozone or UV alone
A persistent free-chlorine residual is automatically formed
A permanent monochloramine residual is generated without ammonia

example.explanation: Neither ozone nor UV treatment leaves a persistent disinfectant residual for the distribution system.

example.prompt: In an aqueous solution model at constant temperature with all other conditions fixed, the hydrogen-ion concentration rises. What happens to the pH value?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: In the aqueous-solution pH model, the pH value falls as the hydrogen-ion concentration rises.

example.prompt: In a water sample where total chlorine equals the sum of free and combined chlorine and free chlorine is held constant, the combined chlorine concentration increases. What happens to the total chlorine concentration?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: Total chlorine is the sum of free and combined chlorine concentrations, so increasing combined chlorine at constant free chlorine increases total chlorine.

example.prompt: In a free-chlorine disinfection model with constant total free chlorine and temperature, the water pH is lowered. What happens to the predominance of hypochlorous acid and microbial inactivation effectiveness?

options.label: Hypochlorous acid becomes more dominant and inactivation is more effective
Hypochlorous acid disappears completely in favour of chloramines
Free-chlorine speciation and effectiveness remain unchanged

example.explanation: At lower pH, hypochlorous acid becomes the dominant form of free chlorine and provides more effective microbial inactivation than hypochlorite ion.

example.prompt: In a treatment model with all other conditions fixed, a chlorine-based disinfectant reacts with organic material present in the water. What disinfection byproducts can form from this reaction?

options.label: Trihalomethanes can form
Diatomaceous earth is formed
Silica sand is precipitated

example.explanation: Trihalomethanes can form when chlorine-based disinfectants react with organic material in water.

example.prompt: In an air-stripping unit with all other conditions fixed, dissolved carbon dioxide is stripped from the water during gas-liquid contact. What happens to the water's pH and tendency for scale formation?

options.label: Both pH and the possibility of scale formation increase
Both pH and the possibility of scale formation decrease
pH and scaling tendency remain unchanged

example.explanation: Removing carbon dioxide during air stripping increases the water's pH and increases the possibility of scale formation.

example.prompt: In a colorimetric DPD chlorine test with all other conditions fixed, the sample contains oxidized manganese. How can the oxidized manganese affect the DPD test?

options.label: It can produce a chlorine-like colour and interfere with the test
It bleaches the sample cell into a primary turbidity standard
It has no effect on DPD colour development

example.explanation: Oxidized manganese can produce a chlorine-like pink colour with DPD and interfere with the chlorine measurement.

example.prompt: In a reagent storage model with all other conditions fixed, DPD reagents are exposed to heat and sunlight. What happens to the shelf life of the DPD reagents?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Exposure to heat and sunlight can degrade DPD reagents and shorten their shelf life.

example.prompt: In a pump suction model with fixed required NPSH and all other conditions constant, the available net positive suction head drops below the pump's required NPSH. What hydraulic phenomenon can occur?

options.label: Cavitation can occur in the pump
The pump automatically becomes an artesian well
Pump suction conditions remain unaffected

example.explanation: Available net positive suction head must exceed the pump's required NPSH to avoid cavitation.

example.prompt: In a small closed pumping system with all other conditions fixed, a pressure tank is included on the discharge side. What happens to the frequency of pump stops and starts?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Pressure tanks in small closed systems provide pressurized volume that reduces frequent pump stops and starts.

example.prompt: In a piped flow measurement model with all other conditions fixed, entrained air enters the water passing through a flow meter. What can happen to the flow meter's accuracy?

options.label: Accuracy can decrease or operation can be disrupted
The meter automatically calibrates itself to a primary standard
Entrained air has no effect on flow metering

example.explanation: Entrained air in the flow stream can reduce a flow meter's accuracy or disrupt its operation.

example.prompt: In a pressurized pumping system with all other conditions fixed, a sudden pump start, pump stop, or power-loss event occurs. What hydraulic effect can this create in the pipeline?

options.label: Hydraulic pressure transients can be created
Water hardness immediately precipitates as sand
Pipeline pressure remains completely static

example.explanation: Abrupt pump starts, stops, and power-loss events can create hydraulic pressure transients in the system.

example.prompt: In a water distribution zone with all other conditions fixed, customer water usage drops to very low levels or passes through oversized pipes and tanks. What happens to the water age in that zone?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: Low usage or oversized pipes and storage tanks increase the elapsed time water spends in distribution, increasing water age.

example.prompt: In a water distribution main with all other conditions fixed, air accumulates at a pipeline high point. What is the hydraulic effect on water flow past that high point?

options.label: Water flow can be impeded
Water flow is accelerated without head loss
High-point air pockets have no hydraulic effect

example.explanation: Accumulated air pockets at a distribution-system high point restrict the cross-section and can impede water flow.

example.prompt: In a treated-water storage tank with all other conditions fixed, thermal stratification develops between warmer and colder water layers. What can happen to vertical mixing and water age in part of the tank?

options.label: Vertical mixing is limited and water age increases in part of the tank
Vertical mixing becomes instantaneous and water age drops to zero
Tank mixing and water age are unaffected by thermal stratification

example.explanation: Thermal stratification can limit vertical tank mixing and increase water age in stagnant parts of the tank.

example.prompt: In a distribution main near a storage facility where settled sediment is present and all other conditions are fixed, a flow reversal occurs. What can happen to the settled sediment?

options.label: Sediment can be mobilized and spread
Sediment permanently bonds into the pipe wall
Sediment vanishes without entering the water

example.explanation: Flow reversals near a storage facility can disturb, mobilize, and spread settled sediment into the flow.

example.prompt: In an enclosed water storage tank with all other conditions fixed, water is withdrawn while tank vents admit air freely. How does admitting air through the vents affect vacuum development inside the tank?

options.label: Vacuum development is reduced
Vacuum development is amplified
Air admission has no effect on internal tank pressure

example.explanation: Tank vents admit air as water is withdrawn, which reduces vacuum development inside the storage structure.

example.prompt: In a steady-flow channel or pipe model with constant wetted cross-sectional area and all other conditions fixed, the average water velocity increases. What happens to the volumetric flow rate?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: Volumetric flow equals wetted cross-sectional area multiplied by average velocity, so increasing average velocity at constant area increases flow.

example.prompt: In a rectangular tank model with fixed length and width and all other conditions constant, the water depth increases. What happens to the contained water volume?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: A rectangular tank's contained volume is length times width times water depth, so increasing water depth at fixed length and width increases volume.

example.prompt: In a cylindrical tank model with fixed water height and all other conditions constant, a tank of larger diameter is used. What happens to the circular cross-sectional area and contained cylindrical volume?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: A circle's area increases with diameter squared and cylindrical volume equals circular area times height, so a larger diameter at fixed height increases both area and volume.

example.prompt: In a steady-volume basin model with fixed contained water volume and all other conditions constant, the volumetric flow rate through the basin increases. What happens to the theoretical detention time?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Theoretical detention time is contained volume divided by volumetric flow, so increasing flow at fixed volume decreases theoretical detention time.

example.prompt: In a tracer travel model over a fixed pipeline distance with all other conditions constant, the travel time required to cover that distance increases. What happens to the calculated average velocity?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Average velocity is distance travelled divided by travel time, so longer travel time over a fixed distance means a lower average velocity.

example.prompt: In a motor-pump efficiency model where motor efficiency is held constant and all other conditions are fixed, the pump efficiency decreases due to wear. What happens to the overall wire-to-water efficiency?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Wire-to-water efficiency combines motor efficiency and pump efficiency by multiplication, so a lower pump efficiency at constant motor efficiency reduces wire-to-water efficiency.

example.prompt: In an ion-exchange softening model where resin holds captured calcium and divalent iron and manganese under fixed conditions, concentrated brine regeneration is applied. What happens to those captured cations?

options.label: They are displaced from the resin into the spent brine
They permanently fuse into the resin polymer matrix
They are converted into gaseous ozone

example.explanation: Brine regeneration displaces captured calcium and divalent iron and manganese from the resin into the spent brine stream.

example.prompt: In an adsorption clarifier model with all other conditions fixed, coagulated water rises through the buoyant plastic media bed. What happens to the floc particles?

options.label: Floc is trapped in the buoyant plastic media
Floc is vaporized into the atmosphere
Floc is converted into dissolved chloride ions

example.explanation: As coagulated water rises through the buoyant plastic media of an adsorption clarifier, floc is trapped within the media bed.

example.prompt: In an ozone-biofiltration train with all other conditions fixed, ozonated water passes through a granular carbon contactor located ahead of a biological filter. What happens to the remaining ozone?

options.label: Remaining ozone is removed before the biological filter
Remaining ozone is concentrated into a persistent distribution residual
Remaining ozone converts the carbon bed into silica sand

example.explanation: A granular carbon contactor placed ahead of a downstream biological filter can remove remaining ozone from the water.

example.prompt: In a hydrogeologic recharge model with all other conditions fixed, infiltrating water penetrates deeper than the shallow soil zone. What groundwater feature can that deeply infiltrating water recharge?

options.label: It can recharge a deeper groundwater aquifer
It immediately evaporates before reaching rock pores
It remains trapped above the ground surface

example.explanation: Water that penetrates deeper than the shallow soil layer can reach and recharge an underlying aquifer.

example.prompt: In a gaining stream reach where the adjacent aquifer water table is higher than the stream surface and all other conditions are fixed, how does water move across the streambed?

options.label: Groundwater enters the stream through its bed
Stream water empties completely into the atmosphere
No water can cross the streambed interface

example.explanation: In a gaining reach, groundwater flows from the adjacent aquifer into the stream channel through the streambed.

example.prompt: In a watershed runoff model with all other conditions fixed, overland runoff erodes and carries soil particles that have phosphorus attached to them. What can happen to that particle-bound phosphorus?

options.label: It can be carried into surface water by the runoff
It sublimates directly into atmospheric oxygen
It is blocked from moving with eroded soil particles

example.explanation: Phosphorus attached to soil particles can be transported into a receiving surface-water body by runoff.

example.prompt: In a benthic sediment model with accumulated organic nitrogen and all other conditions fixed, sediment microbes mineralize the organic nitrogen. What nitrogen species is produced by this transformation?

options.label: Ammonia is produced
Free chlorine is produced
Calcium carbonate scale is produced

example.explanation: During ammonification in sediment, microbes transform organic nitrogen into ammonia.

example.prompt: In an aquatic plant assimilation model with no external ammonia input and all other conditions fixed, algae and aquatic plants actively take up ammonia from the water. What happens to the aqueous ammonia concentration?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: As algae and aquatic plants take up ammonia from the water for growth, the dissolved ammonia concentration in the water decreases.

example.prompt: In a surface-water oxygen transfer model with no oxygen consumption and all other conditions fixed, aquatic plants release oxygen during photosynthesis and atmospheric oxygen absorbs into the water. What happens to the dissolved oxygen in the surrounding water?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: Water absorbs oxygen both directly from the atmosphere and from oxygen released by aquatic plants during photosynthesis, increasing dissolved oxygen.

example.prompt: In an activated-carbon adsorption model with fresh porous carbon and all other conditions fixed, water containing trace organic substances contacts the carbon surfaces. Where do the trace organic substances move?

options.label: From the water onto the activated carbon surfaces
From the carbon pores into atmospheric nitrogen
They remain unable to contact the carbon surface

example.explanation: In carbon adsorption, trace organic substances transfer from the water phase onto the porous activated carbon surfaces.

example.prompt: In an atmospheric rainwater chemistry model with all other conditions fixed, atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolves into rainwater. What acid can form in the water from this reaction?

options.label: Carbonic acid can form
Hypochlorous acid is formed
Sodium hydroxide is formed

example.explanation: When atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolves in rainwater, it reacts with water to form carbonic acid.

example.prompt: In an anaerobic groundwater redox model with sulfate present and all other conditions fixed, sulfate-reducing conditions develop. How is the oxidized sulfur in sulfate transformed?

options.label: It is transformed into reduced sulfide
It is oxidized into dissolved oxygen gas
It precipitates as metallic lead

example.explanation: Under anaerobic sulfate-reducing groundwater conditions, oxidized sulfur in sulfate is transformed into reduced sulfide such as hydrogen sulfide.

example.prompt: In an aquifer model with all other conditions fixed, a well begins pumping and creates a pressure difference around the well bore. How does the surrounding aquifer water respond?

options.label: Surrounding aquifer water moves toward the pumping well
Surrounding aquifer water is repelled away from the low-pressure zone
The pressure difference has no effect on groundwater flow direction

example.explanation: Water in the surrounding aquifer moves toward the pumping well in response to the pressure difference created around it.

example.prompt: In a confined aquifer model where the piezometric level exceeds the land-surface wellhead altitude and all other conditions are fixed, a well taps into the pressurized aquifer. How does water move in this flowing artesian well?

options.label: Water rises through the well and emerges at the land surface without a pump
Water can only be lifted if a high-lift pump is running
Water flows downward from the land surface into the confined aquifer

example.explanation: In a flowing artesian well, pressurized confined aquifer water rises through the well bore and emerges at the land surface without a pump.

example.prompt: In a water-heating model with calcium-bearing hard water and all other conditions fixed, the hard water is heated. What phase change can happen to the dissolved hardness?

options.label: It can form solid calcium carbonate deposits
It converts into volatile organic carbon gas
It permanently turns into soft distilled water without residue

example.explanation: When calcium-bearing hard water is heated, dissolved hardness can precipitate to form solid calcium carbonate scale deposits.

example.prompt: In a premise-plumbing corrosion model with all other conditions fixed, corrosive drinking water contacts susceptible plumbing materials containing lead or copper. What can happen to those metals?

options.label: Lead or copper can transfer into the drinking water
Lead and copper evaporate out of the closed pipe exterior
Corrosive water prevents any metal from entering solution

example.explanation: When corrosive drinking water contacts susceptible plumbing containing lead or copper, metal can leach from the plumbing material into the water supply.

example.prompt: In a UV advanced oxidation process model with all other conditions fixed, UV light reacts with an oxidant to generate radicals in water containing organic contaminants. What do those generated radicals subsequently do to the organic contaminants?

options.label: They oxidize the organic contaminants
They physically strain particles on a microscreen
They create a persistent distribution chlorine residual

example.explanation: In UV advanced oxidation, the radicals generated by the UV-oxidant reaction subsequently oxidize organic contaminants in the water.

example.prompt: In a direct UV photolysis model with no added chemical oxidant and all other conditions fixed, susceptible organic contaminants absorb UV photons emitted from the lamps. What happens to those organic contaminants?

options.label: They are degraded by the absorbed UV photons
They float to the surface on air bubbles
They are exchanged onto anion resin beads

example.explanation: In direct photolysis, photons emitted by UV lamps directly degrade susceptible organic contaminants.

example.prompt: In a conventional clarification train with all other conditions fixed, powdered activated carbon is dispersed into the water upstream of clarification. How does the dispersed PAC leave the water stream?

options.label: It is removed with particulates during clarification
It remains dissolved as a permanent gas residual
It passes into the central collector tube of a spiral-wound RO module

example.explanation: Powdered activated carbon dispersed into water is subsequently separated and removed along with particulates during clarification.

example.prompt: In the conceptual thermal carbon regeneration model with all other conditions fixed, spent carbon granules are cleaned by heating. What can subsequently be done with the thermally cleaned granules?

options.label: The cleaned carbon granules can be reused
The granules become soluble coagulant salts
The granules turn into formazin turbidity standards

example.explanation: Carbon granules that have been cleaned by heating to remove adsorbed contaminants can subsequently be reused.

example.prompt: In a raw-water intake channel at constant flow with all other conditions fixed, debris accumulates on the raw-water screen and increases head loss across it. What happens to the differential water-level measurement across the screen?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: A differential water-level measurement across a raw-water screen reflects its head loss, so higher head loss increases the water-level difference.

example.prompt: In a membrane design sizing model for a fixed target output flow with all other conditions constant, the sustainable membrane flux is lower. How does the membrane area needed to meet that target output change?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: Because the sustainable flux determines how much membrane area is required for a target output, a lower sustainable flux requires a larger membrane area.

example.prompt: In a constant-rate filtration plant with clearwell storage downstream and all other plant inflows fixed, distribution system demand fluctuates over the day. How does the clearwell storage affect the filtration rate?

options.label: Filtration rate remains steadier while storage absorbs demand changes
Filtration rate must instantaneously match every peak distribution draw
Clearwell storage forces the filters to backwash continuously

example.explanation: Clearwell and plant storage absorb distribution demand fluctuations so that constant-rate filters can maintain a steadier filtration rate.

example.prompt: In a drinking-water system model with all other conditions fixed, the utility switches to a different raw-water supply source. What can change in the distribution area served?

options.label: The water's corrosivity can change
The pipe diameters automatically expand
The water's corrosivity is guaranteed to remain identical

example.explanation: Changing a supply source can alter the water chemistry and change the water's corrosivity in the served area.

example.prompt: In a drinking-water biofilter with an established microbial film and all other conditions fixed, water containing biodegradable dissolved organic material passes through the bed. What happens to the dissolved organic material?

options.label: The microbial film helps remove it from the water
It is converted into metallic iron staining
The microbial film has no effect on dissolved organics

example.explanation: A biofilter's microbial film helps remove dissolved organic material as water passes through the bed.

example.prompt: In a water treatment model with all other conditions fixed, ordinary chlorine doses and contact times are applied to water containing Cryptosporidium oocysts. What is the inactivation effect on the Cryptosporidium oocysts?

options.label: They are essentially unaffected by ordinary chlorination
They are completely dissolved into chloride ions
They are instantly inactivated at any free-chlorine level

example.explanation: Ordinary chlorine doses and contact times are essentially ineffective against Cryptosporidium oocysts.

example.prompt: In a water chemistry model with all other conditions fixed, free chlorine reacts with ammonia present in the water. What type of chlorine species is formed?

options.label: Combined chlorine (chloramines)
Dissolved ozone gas
Carbonic acid

example.explanation: Combined chlorine consists of chloramine species formed when chlorine reacts with ammonia.

example.prompt: In a source-water quality model with all other conditions fixed, natural organic matter concentration increases in the water. What aesthetic property can this natural organic matter contribute to the drinking water?

options.label: Colour
Piezometric artesian pressure
Free-chlorine residual

example.explanation: Natural organic matter in water can contribute visible colour to drinking water.

example.prompt: In a distribution water quality model with all other conditions fixed, elevated iron and manganese are present in the supplied water. What aesthetic effects can they cause on fixtures and in the water?

options.label: Brown or black staining as well as visible colour and turbidity
Formation of a persistent UV residual
Complete removal of all water hardness

example.explanation: Iron and manganese can cause brown or black staining as well as visible colour and turbidity.

example.prompt: In a water clarity model with all other conditions fixed, the concentration of suspended silt, organic particles, and inorganic particles increases. What happens to the water's light-scattering turbidity?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: Suspended silt, organic particles, and inorganic particles scatter light and contribute to water turbidity.

example.prompt: In a distribution pipe model with low flow velocity and all other conditions fixed, suspended particles and corrosion products are carried in the water. What can happen to those particles and corrosion products inside the pipe?

options.label: They can settle into distribution-system sediment
They evaporate through the pipe wall into the soil
They convert into free-chlorine residual

example.explanation: Particles and corrosion products in the distribution system can settle out to form pipe sediment.

example.prompt: In a distribution pipe model with no booster chlorination and all other conditions fixed, chlorinated water travels through pipes where chlorine reacts with bulk water constituents, sediment, and pipe-wall material. What happens to the chlorine residual concentration?

options.label: Decrease
Increase
No change

example.explanation: Chlorine reactions in bulk water, settled sediment, and pipe-wall material consume disinfectant residual.

example.prompt: In a rectangular basin surface-area model with fixed basin width and all other conditions constant, the basin length is increased. What happens to the rectangular surface area?

options.label: Increase
Decrease
No change

example.explanation: The area of a rectangle equals length multiplied by width, so increasing length at constant width increases area.

example.prompt: Which statement does not describe raw water before treatment?

options.label: Water before any treatment has been applied
Water moved by low-lift pumping
Water entering raw-water screens
Water carrying a secondary distribution residual

example.explanation: Water carrying a secondary distribution residual has already been treated, while the other options describe untreated raw water.

example.prompt: Which item does not describe the function or monitoring of raw-water screens?

options.label: Removing large solids before downstream treatment
Using differential water level to indicate head loss
Protecting an algae-removal microscreen with a larger-pore prescreen
Inactivating waterborne pathogens prior to distribution

example.explanation: Inactivating pathogens is the role of disinfection, whereas raw-water screens remove large solids, protect microscreens and show head loss by differential water level.

example.prompt: Which statement does not accurately describe dissolved oxygen in water?

options.label: It is oxygen gas dissolved in the water
Cold water can hold more of it than warm water
Bacterial decomposition of organic matter consumes it
It is the oxygen chemically bound inside H2O molecules

example.explanation: Oxygen chemically bound within water molecules is part of the water molecule itself, whereas the other statements describe dissolved oxygen.

example.prompt: Which process does not add dissolved oxygen to water or increase oxygen-holding capacity?

options.label: Direct absorption of oxygen gas from the atmosphere
Oxygen release by aquatic plants during photosynthesis
Colder water temperatures compared with warm water
Bacterial decomposition of organic material

example.explanation: Bacterial decomposition of organic material consumes dissolved oxygen, while atmospheric absorption, aquatic plant photosynthesis and colder water temperatures support higher dissolved oxygen.

example.prompt: Which effect is not a documented result of changing or blending source waters?

options.label: Precipitating iron or manganese when oxygen-rich surface water blends with groundwater
Changing water corrosivity in the served distribution area
Affecting treatment-process selection as seasonal surface-water quality changes
Automatically fixing full-scale filtration rates from a small treatability test

example.explanation: Treatability tests do not automatically set full-scale filtration rates, whereas source changes or blending can alter corrosivity, precipitate iron or manganese, and affect process selection.

example.prompt: Which statement does not describe a limitation of bench-scale jar or small treatability tests?

options.label: They do not automatically provide full-scale reaction times
They do not automatically provide full-scale filtration rates
They may not reproduce full-scale flocculation back-mixing
They cannot inform coagulant or coagulant-aid choices

example.explanation: Informing coagulant and coagulant-aid selection is a valid use of jar tests, whereas the other options state what small tests do not automatically provide.

example.prompt: Which statement about coagulation mixer equipment is not accurate?

options.label: Coagulation mixing can occur in an inline mixer
Coagulation mixing can occur in a separate tank
Powered mixers are a design option when treatment flow varies
Static mixers maintain constant mixing power when flow drops

example.explanation: A static mixer's delivered mixing power can drop substantially when flow decreases, whereas the other statements accurately describe mixer arrangements.

example.prompt: Which statement does not belong to valid flocculation principles?

options.label: Increasing collisions between destabilized particles builds floc
Tapered flocculation decreases velocity gradient from stage to stage
The Gt parameter combines mixing intensity and mixing time
Colour-associated floc is stronger than suspended-turbidity floc

example.explanation: Colour-associated floc is more fragile than turbidity floc, while the other statements accurately describe particle collisions, tapered velocity gradients and Gt.

example.prompt: Which item does not describe conventional gravity sedimentation basins or settler modules?

options.label: Reducing the settleable-solids load on downstream filters
Using tube or plate settlers to enlarge settling area and shorten fall distance
Using surface overflow rate as a principal design parameter
Omitting the sedimentation stage ahead of filtration

example.explanation: Direct filtration omits the sedimentation stage, whereas the other options describe clarification load reduction, settler modules and surface overflow rate.

example.prompt: Which statement does not describe hydraulic and sludge behaviour in a sedimentation or sludge-blanket clarifier?

options.label: Uniform inlet distribution helps prevent hydraulic short-circuiting
Sludge can accumulate more heavily near a sedimentation-basin inlet
A solids-contact clarifier mixes incoming coagulated water with existing sludge
Rapid flow or temperature shifts improve sludge-blanket stability

example.explanation: Rapid changes in water temperature or flow are unfavourable for a sludge-blanket clarifier, while the other statements accurately describe clarifier hydraulics and sludge contact.

example.prompt: Which feature does not belong to dissolved air flotation clarification?

options.label: Treating slowly settling algae-rich or high-colour, low-turbidity water
Providing a contact zone where floc and bubbles meet
Collecting clarified subnatant near the basin floor
Weighting floc with microsand for lamellar settling

example.explanation: Microsand-enhanced flocculation with lamellar settling describes ballasted clarification, whereas the other three features belong to dissolved air flotation.

example.prompt: Which process does not remove or capture particulates ahead of downstream filtration?

options.label: Roughing filter removing coarse particles ahead of slow sand filtration
Adsorption clarifier trapping floc in buoyant plastic media
Ballasted clarification combining microsand flocculation and lamellar settling
Storage tank vent admitting air as water is withdrawn

example.explanation: Tank vents admit air during water withdrawal to prevent vacuum in storage, whereas roughing filters, adsorption clarifiers and ballasted clarifiers capture particles before filtration.

example.prompt: Which statement does not describe granular media filter structure or underdrain function?

options.label: Placing silica sand below anthracite or granular activated carbon in a dual-media bed
Using support media so filter grains do not enter the underdrain
Distributing backwash water or scour air through the underdrain
Building a precoat cake of diatomite on a septum support

example.explanation: Passing water through a supported layer of diatomite describes diatomaceous-earth filtration, whereas the other options describe dual-media beds, support gravel and underdrains.

example.prompt: Which process description does not rely on biological activity on a filter or bioreactor medium?

options.label: Slow sand filtration using an upper-sand microbial layer
A biofilter using a microbial film to remove dissolved organic material
A media-bed bioreactor where bacteria transform contaminants into non-toxic products
Diatomaceous-earth filtration supplemented by a continuous diatomite feed

example.explanation: Diatomaceous-earth filtration physically strains water through a diatomite layer and continuous body feed, whereas the other three rely on microbial films or bacteria on media.

example.prompt: Which statement does not accurately describe membrane filtration performance or maintenance?

options.label: Backwash or reject-stream losses make net output less than feed throughput
Sustainable flux determines the membrane area needed for a target output
A membrane prescreen protects membrane surfaces from damaging debris
Colder water increases membrane flux for a given driving pressure

example.explanation: Colder water can reduce membrane flux rather than increase it, while the other statements accurately describe net output, sustainable flux and prescreening.

example.prompt: Which method is not a direct membrane-integrity test?

Vacuum-hold test
Bubble-point test
Continuous particle counter

example.explanation: A continuous particle counter is an indirect membrane-integrity monitor, whereas pressure-decay, vacuum-hold and bubble-point tests are direct integrity tests.

example.prompt: Which statement does not describe activated carbon adsorption or its use in water treatment?

options.label: Using a porous adsorbent with a large internal surface area
Adsorbing taste-and-odour compounds and disinfection byproduct precursors
Transferring trace organic substances from water onto carbon surfaces
Contacting water with a gas stream to strip dissolved carbon dioxide

example.explanation: Contacting liquid with gas to strip carbon dioxide describes air stripping, whereas the other options describe activated carbon properties and adsorption.

example.prompt: Which statement does not fit the ozone, carbon and biofiltration process relationships?

options.label: Ozone pretreatment makes natural organic matter more biodegradable for a biofilter
A biofilter's microbial film helps remove dissolved organic material
A granular carbon contactor can remove remaining ozone before a downstream biofilter
Ozone provides a long-lasting residual throughout the distribution system

example.explanation: Ozone does not leave a persistent residual for the distribution system, whereas the other statements accurately describe how ozone, carbon contactors and biofilters work together.

example.prompt: Which statement does not accurately describe chlorine demand, residual and CT?

Chlorine residual is the concentration remaining after reactions with impurities
CT equals residual concentration multiplied by effective contact time
Effective T10 is always identical to theoretical hydraulic detention time

example.explanation: Effective T10 can differ substantially from theoretical hydraulic detention time, whereas the other three statements accurately define chlorine demand, chlorine residual and CT.

example.prompt: Which statement does not belong to the chemical disinfection CT and T10 framework?

CT multiplies residual concentration by effective contact time
Effective T10 may differ substantially from theoretical detention time
T10 is the contact time exceeded by only 10 percent of the water

example.explanation: T10 is the contact time exceeded by at least 90 percent of the water, not just 10 percent, while the other options state valid CT relationships.

example.prompt: Which statement does not accurately describe pH, alkalinity or dissolved carbon dioxide chemistry?

options.label: The pH value falls as hydrogen-ion concentration rises
pH is a logarithmic expression of hydrogen-ion concentration
Atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolving in water can form carbonic acid
Alkalinity simply means that a water sample has a basic pH above seven

example.explanation: Alkalinity describes acid-neutralizing capacity rather than simply whether water has a basic pH, while the other statements accurately describe pH and carbon dioxide.

example.prompt: Which statement does not accurately describe aqueous chlorine species?

Total chlorine is usually the sum of free and combined chlorine
Hypochlorous acid dissociates in water to form hypochlorite ion
Free chlorine consists of chloramines bound to ammonia

example.explanation: Free chlorine consists of hypochlorous acid and hypochlorite that have not combined with ammonia, whereas chloramines belong to combined chlorine.

example.prompt: Which statement does not describe iron, manganese or natural organic matter effects in water?

Organic material reacting with chlorine-based disinfectants can form trihalomethanes
Iron and manganese can cause brown or black staining, colour and turbidity
Air stripping removes carbon dioxide, raising pH and scale potential

example.explanation: Removing carbon dioxide by air stripping raises pH and scale potential rather than being an organic or metal staining effect.

example.prompt: Which statement does not belong to the described iron and manganese removal or softening processes?

options.label: An ion-exchange softener can remove dissolved iron and manganese with calcium and magnesium
Brine regeneration displaces calcium and divalent iron and manganese from resin
An oxidant needs reaction time and precipitate formation before membrane filtration
Metal oxidation must be delayed until after coagulation and membrane filtration

example.explanation: In the described pretreatment and membrane models, metal oxidation and precipitate formation occur before coagulation or membrane filtration, not after filtration.

example.prompt: Which statement about colorimetric DPD chlorine testing is not accurate?

An untreated sample blank compensates for the sample's own colour or turbidity
Heat and sunlight can shorten DPD reagent shelf life
Free-chlorine and total-chlorine DPD reagents can be used interchangeably

example.explanation: DPD reagents for free chlorine and total chlorine are not interchangeable, whereas the other statements accurately describe DPD colour development, blanks and shelf life.

example.prompt: Which factor does not cause a false or altered reading in a colorimetric DPD or optical turbidity test?

options.label: Oxidized manganese producing a chlorine-like DPD colour
Bubbles from shaking a colorimeter cell
Smudges, scratches or fog on an optical sample cell
Compensating with an untreated sample blank in a DPD comparison

example.explanation: Using an untreated sample blank compensates for background colour or turbidity, whereas oxidized manganese, shaking bubbles and cell smudges interfere with optical readings.

example.prompt: Which statement does not accurately describe turbidity and nephelometric measurement?

options.label: Turbidity expresses the light-scattering or cloudy character of water
Suspended silt, organic particles and inorganic particles can contribute turbidity
Secondary turbidity standards are made to match primary formazin suspensions
A nephelometer determines turbidity by directly weighing dried solids on a balance

example.explanation: A nephelometer compares scattered-light intensity with a reference suspension rather than directly weighing suspended solids.

example.prompt: Which practice does not preserve sample validity, identity or analytical accuracy?

Applying complete sample labels for traceability through analysis
Calibrating an instrument against a known reference
Rinsing out a pre-preserved sample bottle before filling it

example.explanation: Rinsing a preserved sample bottle can wash out its preservative and invalidate the sample, whereas the other options protect sample integrity and instrument accuracy.

example.prompt: Which statement does not accurately describe water-treatment pumping curves and selection?

options.label: Low-lift pumps move raw water and high-lift pumps move treated water
A pump curve relates flow rate to total dynamic head
Available NPSH must exceed required NPSH to avoid cavitation
Pump selection evaluates only one fixed flow value and ignores head range

example.explanation: Pump selection considers the expected range of flow and head rather than a single flow value alone.

example.prompt: Which statement does not describe a valid pump suction, surge or cycle-control concept?

options.label: A non-flooded suction arrangement may require a priming system
Pressure tanks in small closed systems can reduce frequent pump starts and stops
Slow-opening or slow-closing discharge valves help protect against surge
Sudden power-loss events prevent hydraulic pressure transients in pipelines

example.explanation: Pump starts, stops and power-loss events create hydraulic pressure transients rather than eliminating them.

example.prompt: Which statement about air in pipes, flow meters or storage vents is not accurate?

Tank vents admit air during water withdrawal to reduce vacuum development
Totalizing flow meters record cumulative volume as well as instantaneous flow
Entrained air in a pipe improves flow-meter accuracy

example.explanation: Entrained air can reduce a flow meter's accuracy or disrupt its operation rather than improving accuracy.

example.prompt: Which statement does not describe sediment or chlorine-residual behaviour in distribution systems?

options.label: Particles and corrosion products can settle into distribution-system sediment
Flow reversals near a storage facility can mobilize and spread sediment
Bulk water, sediment and pipe-wall reactions consume chlorine residual
Pipe-wall corrosion products regenerate free chlorine in distribution mains

example.explanation: Chlorine reactions with bulk water, sediment and pipe walls consume residual rather than generating new chlorine residual.

example.prompt: Which formula does not belong to the category of two-dimensional area or three-dimensional volume relationships?

options.label: Rectangle area equals length multiplied by width
Circle area equals pi divided by four, multiplied by diameter squared
Rectangular tank volume equals length times width times water depth
Average velocity equals distance travelled divided by travel time

example.explanation: Dividing distance travelled by travel time gives average velocity, whereas the other three formulas calculate geometric area or volume.

example.prompt: Which mathematical relation does not correctly state an operator calculation formula?

Cylindrical volume equals circular cross-sectional area multiplied by height or length
Wire-to-water efficiency equals motor efficiency multiplied by pump efficiency
Theoretical detention time equals contained volume multiplied by volumetric flow

example.prompt: Which statement does not correctly state a unit conversion or power-energy relationship?

options.label: Unit conversion factors are arranged so that unwanted units cancel
Power measures the amount of work performed per unit time
A kilowatt-hour measures energy used by a power load over elapsed hours
A percent becomes a decimal fraction when multiplied by one thousand

example.explanation: A percent becomes a decimal fraction when divided by one hundred, not when multiplied by one thousand.

example.prompt: Which process does not describe nutrient or sulfur cycling in surface water, sediment or groundwater?
